title: Pozole Rojo
subtitle: Mexican red pork and hominy soup
excerpt: Pozole rojo is a traditional Mexican soup made from pork shoulder and hominy (nixtamalised maize kernels) in a rich red broth of guajillo and ancho chillies. It is eaten at celebrations, on cold days, and as a restorative after long nights. The toppings (shredded cabbage, radish, dried oregano, lime) are as important as the soup itself.
sourceNotes: Pozole has pre-Columbian origins: the Aztecs prepared it using maize and human sacrificial victims on ceremonial occasions. After the Spanish Conquest, pork replaced the sacrificial meat, and the dish became a festive staple throughout Mexico. The three regional versions are rojo (red, most common), verde (green, with tomatillo), and blanco (white, without chilli).

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze without toppings. The soup base improves on reheating.
recipe.batchNotes: Scales directly. Makes a large pot; leftovers reheat perfectly.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The soup is better the next day. Make a day ahead and reheat.

content.text: Tinned hominy (drained and rinsed) is the easiest route in the UK. Dried hominy requires 8 hours of soaking and then 3 hours of cooking before use; tinned is added 30 minutes before the end. The pork should be cooked until it falls apart and can be shredded with two forks. The chilli broth is blended separately and added to the pork broth for depth and colour.

items.prepNote: 1 halved for the broth, 1 finely diced for serving
6 for the broth, 2 for the chilli sauce

content.text: Put the pork shoulder in a large pot with the halved onion, 6 garlic cloves, bay leaves, oregano, and 2 teaspoons of salt. Cover with cold water (about 2.5 litres). Bring to the boil, skim off any foam, then reduce to a low simmer. Cook for 1.5 to 2 hours until the pork is completely tender and pulls apart easily.
Remove the pork and shred it with two forks, discarding any large pieces of fat. Strain the broth and return it to the pot. Discard the spent vegetables.

Toast the guajillo and ancho chillies in a dry frying pan for 30 seconds per side. Cover with boiling water and soak for 20 minutes. Drain and blend with 2 garlic cloves, the cumin, and a ladleful of the pork broth until smooth. Pass through a sieve to remove any skins.
Pour the chilli sauce into the pork broth over medium heat. Stir to combine. Season with salt. Add the drained hominy and shredded pork. Simmer for 30 minutes. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Ladle the soup into deep bowls. Set out the toppings: shredded cabbage, radish, diced onion, dried oregano, and lime wedges. Each diner adds their own. Serve with warm corn tortillas.

items.symptom: Broth is thin and lacks depth
items.cause: The chilli sauce was not enough, or the pork was not simmered long enough to develop flavour
items.fix: Toast more dried chillies, soak, and blend into the broth. Season more aggressively with salt. The broth should taste assertively flavoured before the hominy goes in.
